headline: MILD RED / Narrow Selloff After Two-Day Drop
marketPulseNote: NEPSE closed mildly red on May 13, 2026 at 2740.25, down 4.15 points (-0.15%), extending the two-day losing streak but at a dramatically slower pace than May 12's -1.41% crash. Market breadth remained negative but improved significantly: 82 advances vs 176 declines vs 12 unchanged — far better than yesterday's catastrophic 13/251/5. Total turnover was Rs.2.81B with 5,643,288 shares traded across 42,176 transactions in 339 scrips — roughly 60% of yesterday's volume, suggesting exhaustion of the sell-side. Broker 58 (Naasa Securities) flipped to net BUYER with total purchases of NPR 230,969,464 and total sales of NPR 202,236,622, net +Rs.28.73M. This is a significant reversal from yesterday's -Rs.218.34M net sell. DLBS was the biggest loser at -11.17% (giving back most of yesterday's +15% gain) while AHL led gainers at +11.42%. SYPNL dominated turnover at Rs.277.95M and was the biggest B58 buy target. Manufacturing & Processing (+0.47%) and Trading (+1.50%) were the only green sub-indices.

keyInsights.title: B58 Flips to Net Buyer +Rs.28.73M — Full Reversal from Yesterday
keyInsights.body: After yesterday's massive -Rs.218.34M net sell, Naasa Securities flipped to net buyer today with NPR 230.97M purchases vs NPR 202.24M sales. This dramatic reversal in a single session suggests the May 12 selloff was a planned distribution event followed by selective re-accumulation. Key buys: SAIL (48.03% mkt), RIDI (16.11%), AKJCL (15.70%), SYPNL (11.35%).

keyInsights.title: DLBS -11.17% — Reversal After Yesterday's +15% Gain
keyInsights.body: DLBS followed the same pump-and-dump pattern as FMDBL the session before: +15.00% on May 12, now -11.17% on May 13 at 1,328. This is becoming a recurring pattern — avoid chasing single-day +15% movers in this market.

keyInsights.title: SYPNL Dominant — Rs.277.95M Turnover, B58 Net Buyer
keyInsights.body: SYPNL was the most traded stock today at Rs.277.95M turnover (vs Rs.153.36M yesterday) and rose +4.62% to 1558.90. B58 was a net buyer (20,906 bought vs 16,525 sold). However, RSI is only 46.43 and ADX 29.39 shows a persistent downtrend. The bounce may be technical — treat with caution above 1560.

keyInsights.title: Volume Contraction — Rs.2.81B vs Rs.4.67B Yesterday
keyInsights.body: Total market turnover contracted 40% from Rs.4.67B to Rs.2.81B and shares traded dropped from 10.67M to 5.64M. This volume contraction on a down day is a mildly positive signal — sellers are becoming exhausted. However, a true reversal needs to be confirmed by volume expansion on up days.

keyInsights.title: Manufacturing & Processing +0.47% and Trading +1.50% — Only Green Sectors
keyInsights.body: Mfg & Processing and Trading were the only two sub-indices to close green. SYPNL (Mfg) and RSML/SAIL (Trading) drove these. All other 15 sub-indices remained red, though losses were much smaller than May 12.

keyInsights.title: SOHL Holds +1.02% — Best Large-Cap Hydro on the Day
keyInsights.body: SOHL was the only notable large-cap hydropower stock to close green (+1.02% to 700). ADX 32.41 remains strong, RSI 53.24, AD Osc positive, and B58 bought 8,613 kitta. This stock continues to show the strongest technical structure in the hydro space.

keyInsights.title: SAIL B58 Bought 48.03% of Market — Full Reversal
keyInsights.body: Yesterday B58 sold 15,105 kitta of SAIL (pure sell, 34.41% mkt). Today B58 bought 17,499 kitta (pure buy, 48.03% mkt) — a complete flip. Price recovered +2.05% to 1157.20. This suggests May 12's SAIL sell was profit-taking at a higher level, now being re-accumulated at lower prices.

keyInsights.title: MPFL / NICA / SKHL — Continued or New B58 Distribution
keyInsights.body: MPFL continues to see B58 selling (43.28% of sell side for second day). NICA is a new addition to the distribution list at 29.36% sell market share. SKHL at 32.86% sell market share is also new. These three warrant avoidance until B58 selling subsides.
